name: Expert Knob Twiddlers
editorial_article: Expert Knob Twiddlers is a seminal studio album released in 1996 by the electronic music luminaries Mike Paradinas (better known as µ-Ziq) and Richard D. James (Aphex Twin), operating under the collaborative moniker Mike & Rich. Issued on James’ influential Rephlex Records, the project represents a singular moment in the mid-90s IDM landscape, capturing two titans of experimental electronic music in a remarkably playful, irreverent mood. Recorded largely in 1994, the album emerged as an "updated version of easy listening and funk," marked by idiosyncratic drum programming, whimsical sound design, and a distinct lack of the self-serious tone often attributed to the era's avant-garde electronic producers. \n\nParadinas and James worked quickly on the material, often fueled by late-night sessions and casual experimentation. Tracks like "Giant Deflating Football" highlight the duo's approach: incorporating found-sound textures—such as scraping or blowing into microphones—alongside their signature electronic synthesis. The album's cover art, a parody of the board game Downfall, set the tone for the release, signaling that while the technical prowess was undeniable, the project was fundamentally an exercise in fun. Retrospective critical perspectives have often viewed the record as a "playful, occasionally inspired time capsule," distinguishing it from the more intense or conceptual output typical of the pair's individual discographies. In 2016, the album was rediscovered by a new generation through an expanded reissue via Planet Mu, cementing its legacy as a charmingly unconventional relic of 1990s experimental electronic music.

editorial_pitch: A legendary 1996 collaborative album between electronic icons Aphex Twin and µ-Ziq, Expert Knob Twiddlers showcases the duo’s playful, kitsch-inspired experimentation on Rephlex Records. It is a defining, lighthearted time capsule of the 90s IDM scene.
